# The main flow: idea → ship

```
                       ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                       │  /setup-matt-pocock-skills          │  run once per repo
                       │  (issue tracker, labels, doc paths) │
                       └─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
   ┌────────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ 1.  /grill-with-docs      = /grilling  +  /domain-modeling               │
   │     relentless interview, rounds over a design tree,                     │
   │     writing CONTEXT.md glossary + ADRs inline as decisions land          │
   └────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                    ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
                    │ Can every question be settled in      │
                    │ conversation?                          │
                    └───────┬───────────────────────┬────────┘
                        no  │                       │ yes
              ┌─────────────▼──────────┐            │
              │ /handoff → /prototype  │            │
              │ → /handoff back        │            │
              │ (throwaway code        │            │
              │  answers one question) │            │
              └─────────────┬──────────┘            │
                            └───────────┬───────────┘
                                        │
                    ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
                    │ Multi-session build?                   │
                    └───────┬───────────────────────┬────────┘
                       yes  │                       │ no
       ┌──────────────────▼─────────────┐           │
       │ /to-spec    (synthesise, no    │           │
       │              re-interview)     │           │
       │      ▼                         │           │
       │ /to-tickets (tracer-bullet     │           │
       │   vertical slices + blocking   │           │
       │   edges → tracker)             │           │
       └──────────────────┬─────────────┘           │
                          │  one /implement per ticket,
                          │  /clear between each
                          └─────────────┬───────────┘
                                        ▼
                       ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                       │ /implement                     │
                       │   ├─ drives /tdd internally    │
                       │   │   (one red-green slice     │
                       │   │    at a time, at pre-      │
                       │   │    agreed seams)           │
                       │   └─ closes with /code-review  │
                       │       (Standards ‖ Spec)       │
                       │       then commits             │
                       └────────────────────────────────┘
```

# Skill-by-skill breakdown

| Skill                             | Invocation | Steps / rules, condensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **grilling**                      | model      | 1. Map the request as a **design tree**. 2. The **frontier** = every decision whose prerequisites are settled. 3. Ask the *whole frontier* in one round; number each question; **give your recommended answer** to each. 4. Wait for answers. 5. Recompute the frontier; repeat. Rules: **facts are the agent's job** (dispatch a subagent, never ask the user what you could look up); **decisions are the user's**; a question depending on an open question belongs to a later round; done when the frontier is empty; don't act until the user confirms shared understanding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **grill-with-docs**               | user       | One line: `Call the Skill tool twice, for "grilling" and "domain-modeling"`. (A composition, not a skill.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **domain-modeling**               | model      | Active discipline only (reading `CONTEXT.md` is *not* this skill). 1. Challenge terms that conflict with the glossary, immediately. 2. Sharpen fuzzy/overloaded terms into one canonical term. 3. Stress-test relationships with invented edge-case scenarios. 4. Cross-reference claims against the code; surface contradictions. 5. Update `CONTEXT.md` **inline**, never batched. 6. Offer an ADR only when *all three* hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, result of a real trade-off. `CONTEXT.md` is a glossary and nothing else.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **to-spec**                       | user       | **Do NOT interview** — synthesise what's already known. 1. Explore repo; use glossary vocabulary; respect ADRs. 2. **Sketch the test seams; prefer existing; use the highest possible; fewest possible, ideally one; confirm with the user.** 3. Write spec (Problem / Solution / *long* numbered User Stories / Implementation Decisions / Testing Decisions / Out of Scope / Notes), publish to tracker, label `ready-for-agent`. No file paths or code snippets (they go stale) — except a prototype-derived snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **to-tickets**                    | user       | 1. Gather context (fetch any referenced spec/issue in full). 2. Explore codebase; look for **prefactoring** ("make the change easy, then make the easy change") — becomes its own first ticket. 3. Draft **tracer bullets**: narrow but *complete* path through every layer; demoable alone; fits one fresh context window; explicit **blocking edges**. 4. **Exception — wide refactors**: sequence expand → migrate batches → contract, never a forced tracer bullet. 5. Quiz the user (granularity? edges correct? merge/split?) until approved. 6. Publish blockers-first so edges can reference real ids; native blocking links where the tracker has them. Work the **frontier**. Never modify the parent issue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **implement**                     | user       | Seven lines: implement per spec/tickets; use `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams; typecheck often, single test files often, full suite once at the end; `/code-review`; commit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **tdd**                           | model      | *What a good test is*: verifies behaviour through public interfaces; reads like a specification. **Seams**: the public boundary you test at; tests live at seams, never against internals; **test only at pre-agreed seams, confirmed with the user before any test is written**; highest seam possible; fewest seams. Anti-patterns: **implementation-coupled** (tell: breaks on refactor without behaviour change); **tautological** (assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does — expected values must come from an independent source of truth); **horizontal slicing** (all tests then all implementation). Rules: red before green; one slice at a time; **refactoring is not part of the loop — it belongs to review**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **code-review**                   | model      | Two axes in **parallel sub-agents** so neither pollutes the other. 1. Pin the fixed point; `git diff <fp>...HEAD` (three-dot); verify the ref resolves and the diff is non-empty *before* dispatching. 2. Find the spec (commit-message issue refs → user arg → spec file → ask). 3. Standards sources = repo docs **plus a fixed 12-smell Fowler baseline** (Mysterious Name, Duplicated Code, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Repeated Switches, Shotgun Surgery, Divergent Change, Speculative Generality, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest), each *what it is → how to fix*. Repo docs override the baseline; baseline smells are always judgement calls; skip anything tooling enforces. 4. Dispatch both, 400 words each. 5. Aggregate verbatim under `## Standards` / `## Spec` — **never merge or rerank**, since one axis masking the other is exactly what the split prevents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **diagnosing-bugs**               | model      | **Phase 1 is the skill; everything else is mechanical.** Build a **tight** pass/fail loop that goes **red on this bug**. Ten ways, in order: failing test → curl script → CLI+fixture diff → headless browser → replay a captured trace → throwaway harness → property/fuzz loop → bisection harness → differential loop → HITL bash script (last resort). Then *tighten* it: faster, sharper signal, more deterministic. Non-deterministic bugs: raise the **reproduction rate**, don't chase a clean repro. Completion criterion: **one named command you have already run**, red-capable / deterministic / fast / agent-runnable. "If you catch yourself reading code to build a theory before this command exists, stop." Phase 2 reproduce **and minimise** (cut one element at a time until every remaining element is load-bearing). Phase 3: **3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses** before testing any, each stating its prediction; show the list to the user. Phase 4: one probe per prediction, one variable at a time; debugger > targeted logs > never "log everything and grep"; **tag every debug log `[DEBUG-a4f2]`** so cleanup is one grep; perf regressions measure first. Phase 5: regression test before the fix, **but only if a correct seam exists** — if none does, *that is itself the finding*. Phase 6: six-item cleanup checklist; the winning hypothesis goes in the commit message. Redact every secret first. |
| **codebase-design**               | model      | Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. Glossary used *exactly*: **Module** (scale-agnostic), **Interface** (everything a caller must know — invariants, ordering, error modes, perf, not just the signature), **Implementation**, **Depth** (leverage at the interface), **Seam** (Feathers: alter behaviour without editing in that place), **Adapter** (role, not substance), **Leverage** (callers), **Locality** (maintainers). Principles: depth is a property of the *interface*; **the deletion test** (delete it — does complexity vanish or reappear across N callers?); **the interface is the test surface**; **one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real one**. `DEEPENING.md`: four dependency categories (in-process / local-substitutable / remote-but-owned → port+adapter / true external → mock) determine how the deepened module is tested; **replace, don't layer** (delete the old shallow-module unit tests). `DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md`: spawn 3+ parallel sub-agents, each with a *different* constraint (minimise the interface / maximise flexibility / optimise the common caller / ports-and-adapters), compare on depth, locality, seam placement, then be opinionated.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **improve-codebase-architecture** | user       | 1. **Scope before you scan (YAGNI)** — walk `git log` for hot spots; weight recently-changed code. 2. Sub-agent walks the codebase noting *friction*, not heuristics; apply the deletion test. 3. Self-contained HTML report in `$TMPDIR` (Tailwind + Mermaid CDN), one card per candidate with before/after diagram and a `Strong`/`Worth exploring`/`Speculative` badge; **do not propose interfaces yet**. 4. User picks one → grilling loop, with `CONTEXT.md`/ADR side effects inline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **triage**                        | user       | State machine: 2 category roles (`bug`/`enhancement`) + 5 state roles (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`). Every posted comment starts with an AI-generated disclaimer. Per issue: gather context → run a **redundancy check** (search by domain concept, not the request's wording) and a **prior-rejection check** (`.out-of-scope/*.md`) → recommend and wait → **verify the claim** (reproduce the bug / check the diff does what it claims) → grill if needed → apply outcome. "A PR is an issue with attached code." Triage is only for issues *you didn't create*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **wayfinder**                     | user       | For efforts too big for one session. **Name the destination first** (it fixes the scope). The **map** is one tracker issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, an *index* not a store. Children are **decision tickets** (questions whose resolution is a decision, not slices to execute) sized to one ~100k session, each typed `research` (AFK) / `prototype` / `grilling` / `task`. Native blocking links render the **frontier** visually. **Claim by assigning yourself before any work.** **Fog of war**: don't chart what you can't see — `## Not yet specified` holds the dim view; the test is whether you can *state* the question now, not answer it. `## Out of scope` is a scoping act, never graduates. **Plan, don't do.** Never resolve more than one ticket per session (research excepted).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **prototype**                     | model      | Throwaway code that answers *one* design question. Throwaway is a constraint on how it's written, not a promise to delete it: the prototype is kept as a **primary source** on a `prototype/<name>` branch off main, linked from the implementation issue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **research**                      | model      | Background agent; **primary sources only** (official docs, source, specs, first-party APIs — never a secondary write-up); one cited Markdown file, saved to the repo's existing convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **resolving-merge-conflicts**     | model      | Hunk by hunk, resolving by **intent traced to each side's primary source**, then finish the operation. **Never `--abort`.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **wizard**                        | model      | Generates an interactive bash script for steps only a human can take (provisioning, credentials, CI secrets, third-party dashboards, one-off cutovers) so the procedure stops being re-explained every time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **setup-matt-pocock-skills**      | user       | Run once per repo: choose issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, doc locations. Every downstream skill says "the tracker should have been provided to you; if not, tell the user to run `/setup-…`".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **ask-matt**                      | user       | The router. Maps the main flow, the three on-ramps, codebase health, the two vocabulary layers, standalone skills, and the precondition. Carries `PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### 4b. Matt Pocock — productivity (selected)

| Skill                   | Steps / rules, condensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **writing-for-agents**  | The **two loads**: *context load* (always-resident tokens — descriptions, `AGENTS.md` lines) vs *cognitive load* (the human remembering what exists; "not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency"). The **information hierarchy** ladder: (1) in-file step, (2) in-file reference, (3) disclosed reference behind a pointer. **Progressive disclosure** = moving down the ladder; the test is **branching** — inline what every branch needs, disclose what only some branches reach. **Co-location** within a file. **Sprawl** as the failure mode. **Completion criteria** have two properties: *clarity* (vague bounds invite premature completion) and *demand* (how much they require, which drives latent legwork). **Leading words**: a compact pretrained concept (*tight*, *red*, *tracer bullet*, *fog of war*) repeated as a token, never as a sentence — it anchors execution in the body and invocation in the pointer; coining your own costs you the priors. **Negation is the failure mode beside it**: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it *more* available; prompt the positive. **Pruning**: single source of truth; the environment is a source of truth too (a doc restating `package.json` is a *cache* that goes stale); check every line for *relevance*; hunt **no-ops** (an instruction the model already obeys by default) sentence by sentence and delete the whole sentence; the default fate without pruning is **sediment**. |
| **PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md** | Five options at a boundary, first *yes* wins: (1) **Continue** — rule it out first; costs nothing, loses nothing; yes if the next phase needs this one as a *primary source*, or the smart zone still fits. (2) **`/clear`** if the context is irrelevant to what's next (cheapest move; getting it wrong is one-way — you lose the *why*). (3) **`/handoff`** only for a new harness, new directory, a colleague, or forking a side task mid-phase; what it buys is *portability*. (4) **Subagent** if the task can run AFK. (5) **`/compact`** — the default, deliberately at the *bottom*. Every move except Continue turns a primary source into a lossy secondary one. Make the decision **at** a boundary, never mid-phase.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **handoff**             | Portable markdown to the OS temp dir (not the workspace). Includes a "suggested skills" section. **Never duplicate what a pointer can reach** (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Redact secrets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **wait-what**           | Fire the moment a message doesn't land; re-pitch with the missing context, in plain English, using `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **to-questionnaire**    | Inverse of grilling: interviews you about the *send* (who it's for, what you need back), not the subject.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
